# `mutation-ledger` fixtures — what each one is, and where it came from

`test/mutationledger.test.ts` drives `scripts/mutation-ledger.cjs` over these and never
runs `gh`, so the suite is offline and deterministic. Every log here is an **excerpt of a
real CI run**, not a hand-written one: the figures a test asserts are figures GitHub
actually printed, so a change in cargo's or `node --test`'s output shape reddens the suite
rather than passing against a shape nobody produces any more.

The scrub is the same in every case: the per-test `test … ok` lines are dropped, and
nothing else is edited. What is kept is the `Running` line that names each target, the
`running N tests` line, the `failures:` blocks with their `---- … stdout ----` headers and
panic messages, the `test result:` summary, and the `node --test` TAP trailer. Job, step
and timestamp prefixes are the run's own.

| file | cut from | what it is, and what it discriminates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `green-multitarget.log` | run 33932644347 (green, `a3e54a54`), the `ubuntu-22.04` and `macos-latest` legs | Two jobs × six targets with **six different totals** (594, 25, 280, 0, 3, 2810). A reader that sums `test result:` lines, or takes the first, or ignores the job, gets a different number from each — which is what makes the attribution assertions fail-able rather than decorative. It also carries the two `loomux_server` suites that share a target stem and differ only in `what` (`src/lib.rs` at 25, `src/main.rs` at 0), the collision `suiteLabel` exists for. |
| `red-round13.log` | run 33928069681 (`f9afc965`), round 13 of #2239's wave | The six-test red: `588 passed; 6 failed` in `loomux_engine`, beside that same job's **passing** `node` suite at 2791/0. Two suites in one job, one red — so "pick the failing one" is a choice the fixture can catch getting wrong. |
| `interleaved.log` | run 33937535584 (green on `main` at `2f7744b3`), the `ubuntu-22.04` leg | Three `Running` banners, **two of them adjacent**, with the results arriving in banner order: cargo prints the banner on stderr and the binary prints its own output on stdout, so GitHub’s log interleaves them. Read as "the last banner wins" this gives `loomux_lib` 25 instead of 280 and loses `loomux_server`’s bin target entirely. The suite asserts the collision is really there, so a fixture whose banners and results alternate cleanly cannot satisfy the pin. |
| `red-round1-esc.log` | run 33928049423 (`ce859688`), round 1 of #2239's wave | The one-test red, `593 passed; 1 failed`, **with the real 0x1B escape byte** restored. Every other log here carries the caret notation `^[` that the sandboxed fetch produces. The pair pins that both spellings parse to the same figures; without the caret arm of `stripAnsi` no target is recognised at all and the ledger comes back empty rather than wrong. |
| `truncated.log` | `red-round1-esc.log` with its `test result:` line removed | The **positive control for the zero case**. A log whose test step died, or was cut, or whose target was renamed, yields no totals — and a ledger row with empty figures reads exactly like a round that reddened nothing. `selectSuite` must throw on this, not return a blank row. |
| `node-red.log` | `node --test --test-reporter=tap` over a throwaway file, wrapped in the run-log line prefix | Real TAP from the real runner: 4 tests, `# pass 2`, `# fail 2`, two `not ok` names. `# pass` excludes skips while `# tests` includes them, so neither figure is derivable from the other and both are read. |
| `body-good.md` / `body-stale.md` | #2239's posted ledger, trimmed to the two rounds whose logs are here | The `--check` pair. `body-good` is the **negative control**: a checker that reports everything passes every positive assertion below and fails here. `body-stale` carries five independent stalings, one per checkable figure. |

## Re-blessing

Nothing here is generated by the code under test, so there is no bless step: a fixture is
replaced by cutting a fresh excerpt from a real run and saying in the PR which run, which
job and which rounds. If a fixture is replaced because the *output shape* changed (a cargo
or `node --test` upgrade), say that too — the old excerpt is then evidence about a shape
this repo no longer produces, which is the one reason to retire one.
